standards_review.notes: All 5 commit subjects in range match <type>(<scope>): <subject>; types used (fix, test) are in commitlint type-enum, scopes used (utils, analytics) are in commitlint scope-enum, subjects are imperative-mood and under the 100-char limit.

guide requires Functions under 50 lines/one responsibility and Files under 500 lines; src/cli/commands/analytics/cost/cost-enricher.ts was already 546 lines (over the 500-line limit) and enrichCosts() already spanned ~160 lines before this change; the diff adds a new ~20-line reportedObservedEnd/byFilePath computation block (lines ~419-434) inline into that same oversized function instead of extracting a helper, growing the file to 568 lines. All other touched files (usage-readers.ts, model-normalizer.ts, cost-enricher.test.ts) meet naming, import (.js extensions), explicit-return-type, and logger.debug-not-console.log conventions cleanly.

the guide path named for this check (.ai-run/guides/development/security-patterns.md) does not exist in the repo and no security ArtifactRef was passed, so there is no documented standard to adjudicate against (the repo's actual security guide lives at .ai-run/guides/security/security-practices.md, a different path than specified). Manual inspection of the changed files (cost-enricher.ts, usage-readers.ts, model-normalizer.ts, their test file) found no credential/secret logging, no unsanitized user-controlled paths, and no new injection surface — all logging uses logger.debug with session/model identifiers only.

blocking_findings.violation: code-quality.md: 'Functions: under 50 lines; one responsibility' and 'Files: under 500 lines' — enrichCosts() was already ~160 lines in a 546-line file before this change; the diff adds a new, logically separable reportedObservedEnd/byFilePath grouping block directly into that function rather than factoring it out, pushing the file to 568 lines
blocking_findings.why_blocking: code-quality.md lists function-length/file-length and single-responsibility as blocking standards for this project; adding new logic to an already-oversized function instead of extracting it compounds a documented violation rather than containing it
blocking_findings.remedy: extract the byFilePath grouping and reportedObservedEnd computation (current lines ~419-434) into a small named helper (e.g. computeReportedObservedEnd(ordered: ParsedEntry[]): Map<string, number>) with its own JSDoc, called from enrichCosts, so the new logic has one responsibility and does not grow the existing function
